name: Cuicateco, variedades actuales / present-day Cuicatec varieties
confidence_why: Mendoza Hernández (2023), who collected data in eight Cuicatec communities including the Teutila towns of San Pedro Teutila, Santa María Tlalixtac and San Andrés Teotilálpam, and San Giacomo (2017, 2025) for San Juan Tepeuxila place stress on the syllable that holds the second mora counted from the right edge of the root, while the older Pápalo descriptions (Anderson & Concepción Roque 1983; Needham & Davis 1946) speak of a light stress at the beginning of the root, which picks out the same syllable in ordinary CVCV and CVː roots, so the sources differ in formulation rather than in where stress falls; no published description treats the stress of Teutila Cuicatec on its own.

catalog_quote: [p. 146, sec. 6.4] El acento en las variedades actuales de cuicateco se asigna en la sílaba de la segunda mora a partir del linde derecho los radicales. La asignación del acento suele coincidir con la sílaba prominente en palabras bisilábicas o de mayor extensión. En este sentido, la sílaba que recibe el acento es el lugar donde se facultan las oposiciones y la posición con mayor distribución de segmentos, además de contar con otras propiedades acústicas, como la intensidad y duración (Kager 2007), que las distinguirían de las sílabas no prominentes. Es probable que el cuicateco del Confessonario haya tenido un patrón similar a las variedades actuales para asignar el acento. new_statements.quote: [p.779 §8] Las raíces son monosílabas o bisílabas. Son los morfemas principales. Llevan un acento prosódico muy ligero al principio que se conserva siempre en su lugar de origen aunque estén acompañadas de prefijos. En las raíces monosílabas, además de llevar el acento prosódico, la vocal se alarga más o menos al doble aunque tenga un solo tono. [...] [p.777 §5] En las raíces bisílabas, la vocal de la primera sílaba, la que lleva el acento prosódico, no se alarga [...]. Para el hablante nativo, tanto el acento prosódico como la duración de vocales son fáciles de predecir, y por tal motivo no las señalamos en la ortografía. [p.778 §7, los determinantes] Son de una sílaba, sin acento prosódico, con una vocal corta como elemento central.
new_statements.translation: Roots are monosyllabic or disyllabic. They are the principal morphemes. They carry a very light prosodic accent at their beginning, which always stays in its original place even when prefixes accompany them. In monosyllabic roots, besides carrying the prosodic accent, the vowel is lengthened to roughly double even if it has a single tone. [...] In disyllabic roots the vowel of the first syllable, the one that carries the prosodic accent, is not lengthened [...]. For the native speaker both the prosodic accent and vowel length are easy to predict, and for that reason we do not mark them in the orthography. [Determinants = prefixes, bound pronouns, particles] are monosyllabic, without prosodic accent, with a short vowel as nucleus.
new_statements.citation: Anderson, E. Richard & Hilario Concepción Roque. 1983. Diccionario cuicateco: español-cuicateco, cuicateco-español. (Serie de vocabularios y diccionarios indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 26.) México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. Apéndice A 'Fonología y ortografía'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened the page renders (printed p. 779, sec. 8 'Raices'), -p. 777, sec. 5 'Duracion de las Vocales y Acento Prosodico') and -p. 778, sec. 7 'Determinantes') of Anderson & Concepcion Roque 1983 (scan held by the project). Every quoted sentence is there word for word: p. 779 'Las raices son monosilabas o bisilabas. Son los morfemas principales. Llevan un acento prosodico muy ligero al principio que se conserva siempre en su lugar de origen aunque esten acompanadas de prefijos. En las raices monosilabas, ademas de llevar el acento prosodico, la vocal se alarga mas o menos al doble aunque tenga un solo tono.'; p. 777 'En las raices bisilabas, la vocal de la primera silaba, la que lleva…
new_statements.rule_in_words: A light, predictable word accent falls on the first syllable of the root (roots are (C)V or (C)VCV); it does not shift when prefixes/proclitic 'determinantes' are added, and those elements are never stressed. So prefix+monosyllabic-root words are final-stressed, bare disyllabic roots initial-stressed. Tone (4 levels) is the contrastive prosody; accent is not.
new_statements.exceptions: Apparent CV²CV¹⁴ forms (y'a²ti¹⁴ 'simple', nd'i²cu¹⁴ 'viejo') are explained as compounds with an added tone-4 morpheme, not accent exceptions; the pair cu³ndú¹ 'voy a cardar' (accent on penult: c- + root -u³ndu¹) vs cu⁴ndú²¹ 'voy a montar' (accent on final: cu⁴ + root ndu²¹) shows accent diagnosing the root; Spanish loans keep Spanish stress, realised as fixed tone patterns (pp. 784-785).
new_statements.domain_note: Root/word domain: accent is a property of the root-initial syllable and survives prefixation; illustrated both in citation forms and short verb phrases. CAUTION (identity): the description is of Santa María Pápalo Cuicatec, which ISO 639-3/Ethnologue/SIL catalogue as Tepeuxila Cuicatec [cux] = Glottolog sant1437 under tepe1280; only Glottolog's bibliography attaches this book to teut1235. No stress statement was found for Teutila-proper speech (San Pedro Teutila / San Andrés Teotilalpam).
new_statements.identity_note: All three first-hand stress statements located (Anderson & Concepción Roque 1983; Prewett & Prewett 1972; Needham & Davis 1946) describe Santa María Pápalo or Concepción Pápalo speech. ISO 639-3 / Ethnologue 16 ('Cuicatec, Tepeuxila [cux].. Dialects: Santa María Pápalo') and the SIL archive catalogue both file these under Tepeuxila Cuicatec [cux]; Glottolog has Santa María Pápalo as dialect sant1437 under tepe1280, yet Glottolog 5.1's bibliography attaches the 1983 dictionary to teut1235 (which is why it appears in this target's ref list). The tepe1280 check already uses Anderson 1983, so adopting it here would list one variety under two glottocodes. Teutila-proper (cut: San Pedro Teutila, San Andrés/Santa Cruz Teotilalpam, Santa María Tlalixtac; 'northern/eastern' INALI variants) has open material only in the form of López 1958 word lists; its one modern description (Ariano 2023, San Andrés Teotilálpam consonant system) is print-only.

new_statements.quote: [p. 146 §6.4] El acento en las variedades actuales de cuicateco se asigna en la sílaba de la segunda mora a partir del linde derecho los radicales. La asignación del acento suele coincidir con la sílaba prominente en palabras bisilábicas o de mayor extensión. [p. 47] En la jerarquía prosódica del cuicateco, la formación de la palabra fonológica tiene como requerimiento que el pie métrico tenga un contenido mínimo de dos moras y que el acento se fije en la segunda mora de derecha a izquierda según la exposición de Martínez y Mendoza (2016).
new_statements.translation: [p. 146 §6.4] In the present-day varieties of Cuicatec, stress is assigned to the syllable of the second mora from the right edge of the roots. Stress assignment usually coincides with the prominent syllable in disyllabic or longer words. [p. 47] In the prosodic hierarchy of Cuicatec, the formation of the phonological word requires that the metrical foot have a minimum content of two moras and that stress be fixed on the second mora from right to left, following the account of Martínez y Mendoza (2016).

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the existing statement (Anderson & Concepcion Roque 1983, Santa Maria Papalo: a light prosodic stress at the beginning of the root that stays put under prefixation; monosyllabic roots lengthen their vowel). For Anderson's data the two rules give the same output, since he has CVCV roots with short vowels (stress on the first root syllable) and bimoraic monosyllabic roots. Mendoza adds the mechanism (mora counting from the right edge of the root, two-mora minimal word) and thereby predicts root-final stress when the final root vowel is long, a case Anderson does not describe. Mendoza's statement is explicitly pan-Cuicatec and his 2016-2019 wordlist fieldwork (p. 30) covered th…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the syllable that contains the second mora counting from the right edge of the root (a moraic trochee at the right edge of the root): on a bimoraic monosyllabic root, on the first syllable of a disyllabic root with short vowels, and on the last root syllable if that syllable has a long (bimoraic) vowel. The phonological word requires a minimum of two moras. Stated for 'las variedades actuales de cuicateco' in general; the thesis's own examples (e.g. p. 18-19 ˈkʷekuð 'IRRE-llorar=2PS', ˈnãː 'cara'; p. 141 ˈkaeʔði, ˈkwekoði) and its footnote 143 (p. 123: 'El acento se asigna en la interpretación conforme los patrones actuales de las variedades cuicatecas') apply the same rule to the colonial text.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. The author notes the colonial-text words are longer than modern ones and only says the colonial variety 'probably' had the same pattern (p. 146). The cited source of the rule, Martinez y Mendoza 2016, is not in the thesis bibliography.
new_statements.identity_note: Mendoza 2023 phrases its stress rule for all present-day Cuicatec varieties and its wordlist fieldwork (p. 30) included the northern/Teutila-variant towns San Pedro Teutila, Santa Maria Tlalixtac and San Andres Teotilalpam plus eastern Santa Cruz Teotilalpam, so it is the only opened source whose statement explicitly covers teut1235 communities, though its example forms come from the central variety and the colonial confesionario. The catalog's existing statement (Anderson & Concepcion Roque 1983) is from Santa Maria Papalo, which Ethnologue/SIL file under Tepeuxila Cuicatec [cux] (Glottolog sant1437 under tepe1280) although Glottolog lists the dictionary under teut1235. No Teutila-proper (San Andres Teotilalpam) phonological description with a stress statement is open: Ariano 2023 is print-only.

readall_conflicts: No source contradicts another outright, but the formulations differ. Anderson & Concepcion Roque 1983 (Santa Maria Papalo; the catalog's existing statement, re-read on the page renders: p. 777 sec. 5, p. 778 sec. 7, p. 779 sec. 8) describe a light prosodic stress fixed at the beginning of the root, unaffected by prefixes, with monosyllabic roots lengthening their vowel and CVCV roots having short vowels. Mendoza 2023 (pan-Cuicatec, p. 146) and San Giacomo 2017 (San Juan Tepeuxila, p. 97-98) state a moraic trochee at the right edge of the root, which gives the same placement as Anderson's rule on his data but puts stress on the final root syllable when that syllable has a long vowel (San Giacomo's [βi4ˈkuː3] 'fiesta', [jų3ˈðuː4] 'llano'). Whether Papalo has such long-final-vowel roots cannot be settled from the dictionary, which does not mark length in single-tone roots (Anderson p. 779).. appears to fall on the first', which is consistent with the root-initial description. Mendoza 2023 attributes the rule to 'Martinez y Mendoza 2016', which is absent from his bibliography; San Giacomo cites the same work as 'Mendoza & Martinez 2016'.

sources.note: pp. 777-779 §§5,7,8: roots (mono- or disyllabic) carry a very light 'acento prosódico' at their beginning which stays in place when prefixes are added; 'determinantes' (prefixes, bound pronouns, particles) are monosyllabic and unstressed; monosyllabic roots lengthen; accent and length are predictable and left unwritten; minimal pair cu³ndú¹ (penult accent, root -u³ndu¹) vs cu⁴ndú²¹ (final accent, root ndu²¹). Spanish loans: stress position mapped onto tone patterns (pp. 784-785). Variety: Santa María Pápalo (ISO/SIL/Ethnologue = Tepeuxila cux; Glottolog sant1437 under tepe1280).
